subject: project:gdl
value: EVERY DEFECT THIS LANE FOUND PRESENTED AS AN EMPTY OR GENERIC RESULT, NEVER AS AN ERROR, SO A RETRIEVAL SURFACE MUST BE ABLE TO DISTINGUISH 'NOTHING MATCHED' FROM 'NOTHING WAS ASKED' OR IT WILL BE READ AS A SILENT CORPUS. Four measured instances from one run, all of the same shape. (1) A DERIVED TABLE THAT IS PRESENT BUT EMPTY: `residual_signature` shipped 0 rows against 1001 independently counted, and the only symptom was that every similar-residual query returned nothing -- indistinguishable from a genuine silence. Caught by an independent recount, not by any query. (2) A REGEX WRITTEN FROM ONE EMITTED FORM: the stored corpus signature reads 'opcode multiset IDENTICAL (155/155)' while live `fndiff --ops` emits 'opcode multiset: IDENTICAL (33/33)' with a COLON. A sentinel written from the stored form alone classified all 13 pure-reorder acceptance rows as `empty`, i.e. as carrying no residual at all. Parse BOTH the stored and the live form of any tool output, and fixture both. (3) A CONSTANT LIST READS AS AN ANSWER: a facet every class member shares, or a zero-weight facet that still admits rows, returns a large plausible payload identical for every query. (4) A SPILL STUB THAT CARRIES NO COUNTS lets a programmatic consumer read a 111-row result as an empty graph. CONSEQUENCE, and it is a design rule not a nicety: every derived table needs an INDEPENDENT recount written without the importer's own field readers -- the 92.6% law-citation defect lived inside the field reader, so a check that calls it cannot see a bug inside it -- and every retrieval surface must report what it INDEXED alongside what it MATCHED, so an empty result carries its own diagnosis.
